title: RAW INCOMPLETE: an explicitly named topic with open predicate words and paid scope
summary: An invented small usage language writes the current subject in full and follows it with a variable sequence of assertions and instructions. Four taught property roots can be combined; assertion, making a condition true, prohibition, conditional action and an until-loop remain distinct. New names, properties, relations and actions are written out in ordinary language with explicit type and arity. This is a concrete abstract grammar related to IDEA012, not a new discovery of topic persistence. Its 22-working-sign realization and historical-source interpretation are still unpaid. No native form receives a meaning and no statistics are claimed.

design.mechanism: One explicitly written name selects the subject of subsequent predicate groups. The subject persists until another explicitly written name or a supplied paragraph boundary. Each later group contains one complete assertion or instruction tree, including its scope. A relation's written second participant does not replace the topic. Open vocabulary is retained by full ordinary-language spelling, not by a newly assigned short code.
design.unit: A supplied paragraph of typed, ordered ground statements about explicitly named entities. The writer receives the intended statements, not an unexplained raw historical sentence whose interpretation is assumed solved.
design.contrast: The proposal is neither a fixed seven-field technical record nor a fixed alternation of two tuple words. It does not emit a role word for every field, require a repeated subject in every group, remember the previous field values, or collapse unchanged commands into a REPEAT mark. Its input has a variable number of statements and explicit scope.
design.prediction: After a topic header, every unmarked first argument is exactly that header's named entity. A binary relation or two-argument action never silently changes it. A topicless predicate at paragraph start is invalid. NOT of a property, a goal to make that negative property hold, and prohibition of the corresponding positive goal have different complete parses and meanings.
design.scope: Complete abstract writing and reading rules on a restricted meaningful input domain; incomplete as a 22-sign physical script, unrestricted language or historical recipe compiler. No source or target is encoded, measured or fitted.

input_domain.entities: Named particular objects or portions. Names are nonempty ordinary strings. The same exact name denotes the same stipulated entity within a paragraph; two distinct portions need two visibly distinct names. A new portion is not created by an invisible counter or inferred from another instruction. Entity identity is part of the input, not supplied by an illustration.
input_domain.predicates: Unary properties, binary relations, unary actions and actions with one explicitly named second participant. A quoted predicate label must be an ordinary independently understood predicate of its stated arity, such as green, warmer-than, grind or place-beside. It may not be a private whole-message identifier or an entire encoded clause. A technical term unknown to the reader still needs an external definition or full explanation; merely quoting its letters does not teach its meaning.
input_domain.scope: Ordered assertions, goals, prohibitions, conditional actions, postchecked until-loops and ordered action sequences. Quantification, unresolved pronouns, unspecified antecedents, arbitrary higher arity, numerals with units and tense are not provided. Such input must be explicitly rejected or receive a separately declared grammar; it cannot be hidden inside a short new root.
input_domain.normalization: The intended typed content is preserved. Different original wordings of that identical supplied content need not be recovered. No historical spelling is silently declared semantically irrelevant by this card. Ambiguous historical content requires a separately retained interpretation or alternative before this compiler can apply.
input_domain.paragraphs: Paragraph boundaries are explicitly supplied input and visibly preserved. They clear the topic. A recipe boundary may be used only if explicitly declared to be this input boundary; no native recipe or paragraph identity is inferred. An ordinary physical line wrap changes nothing.
input_domain.literal_domain: Quoted labels and names may contain the inherited 82 ordinary source characters a-z, A-Z, äöüßÄÖÜẞ, digits 0-9, and . , ; : ! ? ( ) - / ' and double quote, plus ordinary spaces. This is a finite spelling domain, not a new extracted alphabet. An unsupported character produces a visible unsupported-input stop; nothing is deleted. Backslash is reserved as an escape in the teaching syntax rather than accepted as input content.

teaching_syntax.warning: All following characters and root values are artificial explanatory notation, not Voynich sign assignments. Spaces inside quotes are visibly quoted content. Outside quotes, an ordinary space separates complete abstract groups. Thus a quoted multiword name may require several physical words in a future carrier; the card does not count it as one native word for free.
teaching_syntax.quote: A string is enclosed in double quotes. A literal double quote inside it is written as backslash followed by double quote. No other escape is legal. Parentheses, commas, spaces and root letters inside a quote are literal. Empty names and empty predicate labels are invalid. The closing quote is paid and cannot be inferred from the desired interpretation.
teaching_syntax.topic: @ followed by a quoted name is one topic group, for example @"Nara". It introduces no assertion or action. The name becomes the first argument of every following statement until an explicit new topic or paragraph boundary.
teaching_syntax.open_atoms: p followed by a quoted unary-property label is an atom. r followed by a quoted binary-relation label and a parenthesized quoted entity name is an atom: r"warmer-than"("Vela"). Its first argument is the current topic and its second is the named entity.
teaching_syntax.property_grammar: P := one or more adjacent atoms | !(P) | &(P,P). An atom is W, D, F, C, p"label", or r"label"("name"). An adjacent atom run is an ordered conjunction. Nested general conjunction uses the visible &( , ) form. NOT has exactly one parenthesized property operand. A mixed string such as W!(D) is invalid; it must be &(W,!(D)).
teaching_syntax.assertion: A complete P written as a group asserts P of the current topic. WD asserts warm and dry. WW is a legal conjunction with two occurrences of the same assertion. No additional quantity, plural, intensity, iteration or contrast is inferred from that duplication. Both occurrences remain in the recovered content tree; their truth conditions can coincide.
teaching_syntax.action_grammar: A := g(P) | a1"label" | a2"label"("name") | b(A) | i(P,A) | u(A,P) | s(A,A). Every prefix has fixed arity and visible parentheses where shown. An entire A is one abstract instruction group. The digits in a1 and a2 are written type labels, not inferred arity.

action_meanings.g: Bring about the stated property of the current topic. The method is not specified. g(F) means make fine, not grind, chop or sieve; a required method must be written as a named action.
action_meanings.a1: Perform the fully named unary action on the current topic. a1"grind" pays the normal word grind; it does not invent a new compact grind root.
action_meanings.a2: Perform the fully named action on the current topic with the written second entity, in that order. The second entity does not become the next topic.
action_meanings.b: Forbid its complete action operand. It is a directive about that action, not a statement that a property is false.
action_meanings.i: If the stated property of the current topic holds, perform the complete action operand once; otherwise perform no action. No unstated else branch is supplied.
action_meanings.u: Perform the complete action operand once, then check its property operand on the current topic; repeat that action while the condition is false. The first action is compulsory even if the condition held initially. This postchecked convention is explicit and cannot silently replace a source instruction with different loop timing.
action_meanings.s: Perform the first complete action and then the second, preserving both and their order. This supplies explicit scope for a multi-step action inside IF, UNTIL or a prohibition.

teaching_syntax.grouping: One supplied assertion or instruction tree yields one complete abstract predicate group. A supplied topic introduction yields one header. Consecutive input statements are never automatically fused, deduplicated or separated according to their output shape. A source assertion containing an ordered list of simple properties uses the atom run; general Boolean structure remains explicit. Grouping is therefore fixed by the declared input tree, which must itself be paid before any source experiment.

writing_steps: Begin a supplied paragraph with no topic. Write its first required entity name in full after @. A predicate before such a header is an error.

For each supplied statement, confirm that its first entity is the current topic. If not, write a new @ name header before it. Never borrow an implicit entity from an image, a previous paragraph or the last relation's second argument.

Use W, D, F or C only for those four stipulated properties. Write every other property, relation or action label in full with its type and required second argument. Retain every NOT, IF, UNTIL and action-sequence node with the shown delimiters.

Write one group for the complete statement and then its boundary. Repeated complete statements are written again unchanged; there is no mandatory repeat code and no memory of previously true properties that licenses omission.

Wrap only between complete abstract groups. A wrap neither changes the topic nor changes the spelling. A group wider than the available line needs a separately declared physical continuation convention; this card supplies no free within-group line break.
At a visible supplied paragraph boundary clear the topic. The next paragraph must name its first entity again.
reading_steps: Read quotes and their one escape rule literally. Distinguish quoted content from grammar delimiters before interpreting any root or operator.
On @"name", store exactly that named entity. Reject a predicate when no topic has been written in the current paragraph.

Parse each property or action using the disjoint initial tags, fixed operator arities and explicit delimiters. Expand every short property root to its taught property; retain fully written open labels and named arguments.
Insert the stored topic as the first argument of each property, relation and action node in this complete statement. Do not update it from a relation's second participant or an action's object.

Return the ordered content trees, including repeated roots, repeated statements and exact scope. Recovering a particular earlier natural-language spelling is neither promised nor needed for this declared content input.
Clear the stored topic only at the visible supplied paragraph boundary or replace it at a new explicit @ header.

invented_complete_examples.teaching_text: @"Nara" WD b(g(W)) i(!(D),u(a1"stir",D)) r"warmer-than"("Vela") C @"Vela" g(!(W))
invented_complete_examples.complete_reading: Nara is warm and dry. Do not make Nara warm. If Nara is not dry, stir Nara at least once and continue stirring until Nara is dry. Nara is warmer than Vela. Nara is clean. Concerning Vela now: make Vela not warm.
invented_complete_examples.scope_check: The C after the comparison is still about Nara. Only the following explicit Vela header changes the topic. The first prohibition and the last negative goal remain different instructions. The source is wholly invented; no Voynich word has received any value.

invented_complete_examples.complete_reading: Nara is warm. Nara is warm and Nara is warm. Nara is warm. Turn Nara. Turn Nara again as a second explicitly repeated instruction.
invented_complete_examples.scope_check: The repeated bare property and compound do not trigger an implicit nominal argument, plurality or a new portion. The two identical whole action groups remain two ordered commands. This shows abstract representability only; W is not a native glyph or word and no BB-to-native alignment follows.

invented_complete_examples.complete_reading: Neruna is green. Place Neruna beside Velari. Make Neruna fine in texture.
invented_complete_examples.scope_check: Both invented entity names and the unlisted property and action are fully spelled. The final goal still concerns Neruna. It does not specifically say to grind it; a required grinding action would have to be written explicitly.

paid_costs_and_open_debt.learning: Four property-root meanings; topic introduction; two open predicate types; NOT and general conjunction; seven action constructions g/a1/a2/b/i/u/s with their fixed arities and loop convention; the quote/escape rule. Ordinary language vocabulary is still required to understand quoted labels. This is a small additional grammar, not a four-word universal language.
paid_costs_and_open_debt.memory: One explicitly introduced topic name, plus the ordinary nesting stack required by the visible syntax. Deeply nested clauses are not claimed easy. The reader may refer back to the written name rather than memorize an arbitrarily long label, which is a real page lookup cost. No fixed-size four-name cache or hidden prior-record table is assumed.
paid_costs_and_open_debt.open_vocabulary: Each new entity and new predicate costs its entire spelling plus type, quotation, argument and scope marks. New names are not automatically abbreviated or normalized. A long unique name may dominate the written length. No claim is made to rescue1175's open-name cost.
paid_costs_and_open_debt.carrier: There is NO frozen mapping of the teaching grammar, its punctuation and its open spelling to the22working signs. A future realization must pay for all controls, name characters, word boundaries, literal escapes and long-group continuation together. Counting the explanatory syntax as if every label were one native sign would be invalid. No standalone candidate is selected until that debt is resolved.
paid_costs_and_open_debt.source_interpretation: The compiler consumes explicit content trees. Deriving such a tree from a real historical sentence, distinguishing property from action, and deciding which pronoun denotes which entity are additional substantive tasks. This card supplies no historical translator and does not presume a Voynich source language.

design.smallest_decision_changing_consequence: In the invented sequence @Nara, relation(Nara,Vela), CLEAN, the final subject is necessarily Nara. If the intended last clause concerns Vela, the unchanged writer must include a new explicit Vela header. A putative realization requiring subject change at an unmarked second argument is a different grammar. Before any corpus/statistical trial, a table-only manual reading must preserve this contrast and distinguish b(g(W)) from g(!(W)) and !(W). Failure would close this particular topic/scope contract independently of whether its form frequencies look convenient.
known_counterexamples_and_limits: No topic principle is new here: IDEA012 already proposes a continuing record topic. The additional work is an explicit invented producer/parser with fully written introduction, typed open labels and strict scope. Its existence does not validate the old native topic hypothesis.

Known native whole-word doublets with different initials, diverse y/r/l terminals and the ol/olol family are requirements for an eventual carrier. This abstract language permits repeated whole statements and repeated property atoms, but that is not evidence that a22-sign realization fits those actual forms. It claims no successful native binding.

Unlike947, a short property group is already a complete assertion about an explicitly introduced topic; it is not a doubled action head waiting for a strictly nominal next group. That is a deliberately different whole grammar, not a repair or reopening of947's failed fixed parser.

The explanatory syntax has many closing parentheses or quotes. No argument is offered that their literal treatment has the observed native terminal diversity. Removing or changing them later would require a separately paid unambiguous carrier, not an assertion that punctuation is free.

A meaningful assertion may be redundant or contradictory. The writer retains it instead of selecting a short state-dependent form or deleting it. Logical truth and practical execution are not validated by reversible syntax.

No frequency screen on1174's finite uniform tuples or on the four historical source projections is run or passed. Repartitioning those old records into this new content grammar cannot be treated as a free post-result repair. The required content compilation and source contract must be fixed before any such comparison.

predecessors_and_limits.relation: Closest existing topic family. Its record-initial whole and continuing owner/topic idea remains dependent on independently bound records and topic changes. The present card retains that conceptual ancestry and constructs only an artificial source-side grammar; no native novelty or reopening is claimed.

Earlier editions rendered carried arguments and completed owners using source traces, owner classes and defaults. Those exploratory voices and later divergences do not provide confirmed native meanings. This grammar requires its one topic to be visibly named by its own text and does not inherit their owner values or completion defaults.

Finite role-word prototypes and942's common injective two-tuple organization remain failed on their fixed content. Here there is no fixed field count, repeated plant identity or mandatory alternating tuple pair. This difference is a new input/grammar obligation, not a claim that any old source-frequency gate is now satisfied.

The old B6 grammar's literal costs and exact short-square exclusion, and947's action-head/nominal-argument contradiction, are retained. This card neither adds roots to that parser nor changes its arities. Full open labels are explicitly costly, and bare topic properties have a newly declared complete-clause role only in this separate invented language.

The reusable-part and content-equivalent composition questions are older. An abstract conjunction containing a property twice does not identify native reduplication, require a unique internal morpheme parse, or assign a numerical/plural reading. The present teaching grammar is only one stipulated content algebra.
